To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the crust in the western U.S. Basin and Range province is thinned by 30–40% and that the lithosphere in the Colorado Plateau region is thinned by about 50% compared to the adjacent Rocky Mountains and Basin and Range.

(1) the crustal thinning in the Basin andRange province is not uniform but is concentrated in a 50–200 km wide zone that extends from the east limit of normal faults that account of more than 10% extension to the east limit of crustal thinning beneath the plateau and (2) the crustal shear zone in the Basin and range province is a simple shear zone that extends to a depth of about 50 km and that the crust in the zone was moved
the continental lithosphere can undergo large uniform-sense normal shear, with the crust being dragged along by the lithosphere.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature and causes of crustal extension in western North America.
the nature and extent of the lithosphere and the processes responsible for its deformation and evolution.
the nature of continental extensional systems and their relationship to the formation of continental crust.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lithosphere in Arizona and Utah is being uniformly extended in a simple shear sense, with the crustal component of that shear being accommodated by low-angle normal faulting and crustal thinning.

the entire lithosphere failed in Arizona and Utah, moving lower and upper crustal rocks that were initially within the discrepant zone up-and-to-the-east to where they now locally are exposed in the Basin Range Province.
the entire lithosphere, including the upper mantle, is being uniformly and continuously sheared in the east-directed, down-to-the-east sense in Arizona, Utah, the Red Sea, and possibly Death Valley.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
uniform-sense normal shear is a viable mechanism for the extensional tectonic history of the Colorado Plateaus and Basin and Range region.
uniform-sense normal crustal simple shear of the lithosphere is an important process in continental extension.
the lithosphere has undergone uniform-sense normal shear, moving the lower crust and upper mantle up-and-to-the-east relative to the overlying upper crust.
The main takeaway from our work is that

large-scale uniform-sense shear of the lithosphere is a viable mechanism for continental extension, and it is a mechanism that can be used to understand the evolution of the lithosphere in other tectonic settings.
the crust is not the only layer in the lithosphere that can thin.
the lithosphere can be extended by simple-shear, which can be accommodated by a single fault or a series of faults.
